<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

This PR updates npm dependencies across 3 directories in the computeruse package, primarily updating `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` from various versions (1.17.3, 1.25.0) to 1.26.0. The update includes critical security fixes and addresses multiple vulnerabilities.

**Key Security Improvements:**
- **`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.26.0**: Fixes GHSA-345p-7cg4-v4c7 (cross-client response data leak vulnerability), prevents ReDoS attacks in UriTemplate regex patterns, and resolves npm audit vulnerabilities
- **`ajv` 6.12.6→8.18.0**: Major version upgrade with CVE-2025-69873 fix (ReDoS mitigation in pattern validation with $data keyword)
- **`qs` 6.14.0→6.15.0**: Minor update with bug fixes for arrayLimit handling and strictMerge option
- **`hono` 4.11.1→4.12.0**: Minor update with performance improvements (transitive dependency)

**Breaking Change Analysis:**
The `ajv` major version bump (v6→v8) is a transitive dependency change brought in by `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`. Since the codebase does not directly import or use `ajv` (verified via code search), this breaking change is internally handled by the SDK and poses no risk to the application code.

**Compatibility:**
The MCP SDK v1.26.0 maintains backward compatibility with v1.x APIs. The update includes type fixes and additional features (client credentials scopes support, schema validation improvements) without breaking existing usage patterns.

<h3>Confidence Score: 5/5</h3>

- This PR is safe to merge with no risk - it's an automated dependency update that addresses critical security vulnerabilities
- Score of 5 reflects: (1) automated Dependabot PR with well-documented changes, (2) critical security fixes including GHSA advisory and CVE patches, (3) no direct code changes - only dependency version bumps in lock files, (4) ajv major version bump is safely encapsulated within @modelcontextprotocol/sdk with no direct usage in application code, (5) all updates maintain backward compatibility for the SDK's public API
- No files require special attention - all changes are standard dependency updates in package.json and package-lock.json files

<details>
<summary>Changelog</summary>
<p><em>Sourced from <a href="https://github.com/ljharb/qs/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md">qs's changelog</a>.</em></p>
<blockquote>
<h2><strong>6.15.0</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li>[New] <code>parse</code>: add <code>strictMerge</code> option to wrap object/primitive conflicts in an array (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/425">#425</a>, <a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/122">#122</a>)</li>
<li>[Fix] <code>duplicates</code> option should not apply to bracket notation keys (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/514">#514</a>)</li>
</ul>
<h2><strong>6.14.2</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li>[Fix] <code>parse</code>: mark overflow objects for indexed notation exceeding <code>arrayLimit</code> (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/546">#546</a>)</li>
<li>[Fix] <code>arrayLimit</code> means max count, not max index, in <code>combine</code>/<code>merge</code>/<code>parseArrayValue</code></li>
<li>[Fix] <code>parse</code>: throw on <code>arrayLimit</code> exceeded with indexed notation when <code>throwOnLimitExceeded</code> is true (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/529">#529</a>)</li>
<li>[Fix] <code>parse</code>: enforce <code>arrayLimit</code> on <code>comma</code>-parsed values</li>
<li>[Fix] <code>parse</code>: fix error message to reflect arrayLimit as max index; remove extraneous comments (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/545">#545</a>)</li>
<li>[Robustness] avoid <code>.push</code>, use <code>void</code></li>
<li>[readme] document that <code>addQueryPrefix</code> does not add <code>?</code> to empty output (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/418">#418</a>)</li>
<li>[readme] clarify <code>parseArrays</code> and <code>arrayLimit</code> documentation (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/543">#543</a>)</li>
<li>[readme] replace runkit CI badge with shields.io check-runs badge</li>
<li>[meta] fix changelog typo (<code>arrayLength</code> → <code>arrayLimit</code>)</li>
<li>[actions] fix rebase workflow permissions</li>
</ul>
<h2><strong>6.14.1</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li>[Fix] ensure <code>arrayLimit</code> applies to <code>[]</code> notation as well</li>
<li>[Fix] <code>parse</code>: when a custom decoder returns <code>null</code> for a key, ignore that key</li>
<li>[Refactor] <code>parse</code>: extract key segment splitting helper</li>
<li>[meta] add threat model</li>
<li>[actions] add workflow permissions</li>
<li>[Tests] <code>stringify</code>: increase coverage</li>
<li>[Dev Deps] update <code>eslint</code>, <code>@ljharb/eslint-config</code>, <code>npmignore</code>, <code>es-value-fixtures</code>, <code>for-each</code>, <code>object-inspect</code></li>
</ul>
</blockquote>

<h2><strong>6.15.0</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li>[New] <code>parse</code>: add <code>strictMerge</code> option to wrap object/primitive conflicts in an array (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/425">#425</a>, <a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/122">#122</a>)</li>

<h2><strong>6.14.2</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li>[Fix] <code>parse</code>: mark overflow objects for indexed notation exceeding <code>arrayLimit</code> (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/546">#546</a>)</li>

<li>[meta] fix changelog typo (<code>arrayLength</code> → <code>arrayLimit</code>)</li>
<li>[actions] fix rebase workflow permissions</li>
</ul>
<h2><strong>6.14.1</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li>[Fix] ensure <code>arrayLimit</code> applies to <code>[]</code> notation as well</li>

<h2>v4.12.1</h2>

</ul>
<p><strong>Full Changelog</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/honojs/hono/compare/v4.12.0...v4.12.1">https://github.com/honojs/hono/compare/v4.12.0...v4.12.1</a></p>
<h2>v4.12.0</h2>
<h1>Release Notes</h1>
<p>Hono v4.12.0 is now available!</p>
<p>This release includes new features for the Hono client, middleware improvements, adapter enhancements, and significant performance improvements to the router and context.</p>
<h2><code>$path</code> for Hono Client</h2>
<p>The Hono client now has a <code>$path()</code> method that returns the path string instead of a full URL. This is useful when you need just the path portion for routing or key-based operations:</p>
<pre lang="ts"><code>const client = hc&lt;typeof app&gt;('http://localhost:8787')
<p>// Get the path string
const path = client.api.posts.$path()
// =&gt; '/api/posts'</p>
<p>// With path parameters
const postPath = client.api.posts[':id'].$path({
param: { id: '123' },
})
// =&gt; '/api/posts/123'</p>
<p>// With query parameters
const searchPath = client.api.posts.$path({
query: { filter: 'test' },
})
// =&gt; '/api/posts?filter=test'
</code></pre></p>
<p>Unlike <code>$url()</code> which returns a <code>URL</code> object, <code>$path()</code> returns a plain path string, making it convenient for use with routers or as cache keys.</p>
<p>Thanks <a href="https://github.com/ShaMan123"><code>@​ShaMan123</code></a>!</p>
<h2><code>ApplyGlobalResponse</code> Type Helper for RPC Client</h2>
<p>The new <code>ApplyGlobalResponse</code> type helper allows you to add global error response types to all routes in the RPC client. This is useful for typing common error responses from <code>app.onError()</code> or global middlewares:</p>
<pre lang="ts"><code>const app = new Hono()
  .get('/api/users', (c) =&gt; c.json({ users: ['alice', 'bob'] }, 200))
  .onError((err, c) =&gt; c.json({ error: err.message }, 500))
&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt; 
</code></pre>
</blockquote>
<p>... (truncated)</p>

</ul>
<p><strong>Full Changelog</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/honojs/hono/compare/v4.11.7...v4.11.8">https://github.com/honojs/hono/compare/v4.11.7...v4.11.8</a></p>
<h2>v4.11.7</h2>
<h1>Security Release</h1>
<p>This release includes security fixes for multiple vulnerabilities in Hono and related middleware. We recommend upgrading if you are using any of the affected components.</p>
<h2>Components</h2>
<h3>IP Restriction Middleware</h3>
<p>Fixed an IPv4 address validation bypass that could allow IP-based access control to be bypassed under certain configurations.</p>
<h3>Cache Middleware</h3>
<p>Fixed an issue where responses marked with <code>Cache-Control: private</code> or <code>no-store</code> could be cached, potentially leading to information disclosure on some runtimes.</p>
<h3>Serve Static Middleware (Cloudflare Workers adapter)</h3>
<p>Fixed an issue that could allow unintended access to internal asset keys when serving static files with user-controlled paths.</p>
<h3>hono/jsx <code>ErrorBoundary</code></h3>
<p>Fixed a reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) issue in the <code>ErrorBoundary</code> component that could occur when untrusted strings were rendered without proper escaping.</p>
<h2>Recommendation</h2>
<p>Users are encouraged to upgrade to this release, especially if they:</p>
<ul>
<li>Use IP Restriction Middleware</li>
<li>Use Cache Middleware on Deno, Bun, or Node.js</li>
<li>Use Serve Static Middleware with user-controlled paths on Cloudflare Workers</li>
<li>Render untrusted data inside <code>ErrorBoundary</code> components</li>
</ul>

<h2>Greptile Overview</h2>

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

Updated `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` from 1.17.3 to 1.26.0 across 3 directories (main agent, integration tests, and example client), addressing critical security vulnerability GHSA-345p-7cg4-v4c7 where shared server/transport instances could leak cross-client response data.

**Key Changes:**
- Main package upgraded from 1.17.3 → 1.26.0 (security patch addressing response data leakage)
- Example client upgraded from 1.25.1 → 1.26.0 (minor version jump)
- Transitive dependency updates include `hono` 4.11.1 → 4.11.9 (security release fixing XSS, cache middleware, IP restriction, and static file access issues) and `qs` 6.14.0 → 6.14.1 (fixes for array length handling and ReDoS prevention)
- All changes are backwards-compatible within semver caret ranges

**Security Improvements:**
- Fixes critical data leakage vulnerability in MCP SDK
- ReDoS prevention in UriTemplate regex patterns
- Hono security patches for XSS, cache control, IP validation, and asset access
- Improved client sampling validation

The update is standard Dependabot maintenance with important security fixes. Code using the SDK APIs (`Client`, `StdioClientTransport`, `ElicitRequestSchema`, etc.) remains compatible as these are non-breaking updates within the v1.x line.

<h3>Confidence Score: 5/5</h3>

- This PR is safe to merge with minimal risk
- This is a standard Dependabot security update that addresses critical vulnerabilities in `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and transitive dependencies. All updates follow semver, remain within declared caret ranges, and include important security patches. The SDK changes are backwards-compatible (v1.x line), and the existing code using Client, StdioClientTransport, and related APIs will continue to work without modification.
- No files require special attention

Updates `qs` from 6.14.0 to 6.15.0
<details>
<summary>Changelog</summary>
<p><em>Sourced from <a href="https://github.com/ljharb/qs/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md">qs's changelog</a>.</em></p>
<blockquote>
<h2><strong>6.15.0</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li>[New] <code>parse</code>: add <code>strictMerge</code> option to wrap object/primitive conflicts in an array (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/425">#425</a>, <a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/122">#122</a>)</li>
<li>[Fix] <code>duplicates</code> option should not apply to bracket notation keys (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/514">#514</a>)</li>
</ul>
<h2><strong>6.14.2</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li>[Fix] <code>parse</code>: mark overflow objects for indexed notation exceeding <code>arrayLimit</code> (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/546">#546</a>)</li>
<li>[Fix] <code>arrayLimit</code> means max count, not max index, in <code>combine</code>/<code>merge</code>/<code>parseArrayValue</code></li>
<li>[Fix] <code>parse</code>: throw on <code>arrayLimit</code> exceeded with indexed notation when <code>throwOnLimitExceeded</code> is true (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/529">#529</a>)</li>
<li>[Fix] <code>parse</code>: enforce <code>arrayLimit</code> on <code>comma</code>-parsed values</li>
<li>[Fix] <code>parse</code>: fix error message to reflect arrayLimit as max index; remove extraneous comments (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/545">#545</a>)</li>
<li>[Robustness] avoid <code>.push</code>, use <code>void</code></li>
<li>[readme] document that <code>addQueryPrefix</code> does not add <code>?</code> to empty output (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/418">#418</a>)</li>
<li>[readme] clarify <code>parseArrays</code> and <code>arrayLimit</code> documentation (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/543">#543</a>)</li>
<li>[readme] replace runkit CI badge with shields.io check-runs badge</li>
<li>[meta] fix changelog typo (<code>arrayLength</code> → <code>arrayLimit</code>)</li>
<li>[actions] fix rebase workflow permissions</li>
</ul>
<h2><strong>6.14.1</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li>[Fix] ensure <code>arrayLimit</code> applies to <code>[]</code> notation as well</li>
<li>[Fix] <code>parse</code>: when a custom decoder returns <code>null</code> for a key, ignore that key</li>
<li>[Refactor] <code>parse</code>: extract key segment splitting helper</li>
<li>[meta] add threat model</li>
<li>[actions] add workflow permissions</li>
<li>[Tests] <code>stringify</code>: increase coverage</li>
<li>[Dev Deps] update <code>eslint</code>, <code>@ljharb/eslint-config</code>, <code>npmignore</code>, <code>es-value-fixtures</code>, <code>for-each</code>, <code>object-inspect</code></li>
</ul>
</blockquote>
</details>

<h2>v4.11.7</h2>
<h1>Security Release</h1>
<p>This release includes security fixes for multiple vulnerabilities in Hono and related middleware. We recommend upgrading if you are using any of the affected components.</p>
<h2>Components</h2>
<h3>IP Restriction Middleware</h3>
<p>Fixed an IPv4 address validation bypass that could allow IP-based access control to be bypassed under certain configurations.</p>
<h3>Cache Middleware</h3>
<p>Fixed an issue where responses marked with <code>Cache-Control: private</code> or <code>no-store</code> could be cached, potentially leading to information disclosure on some runtimes.</p>
<h3>Serve Static Middleware (Cloudflare Workers adapter)</h3>
<p>Fixed an issue that could allow unintended access to internal asset keys when serving static files with user-controlled paths.</p>
<h3>hono/jsx <code>ErrorBoundary</code></h3>
<p>Fixed a reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) issue in the <code>ErrorBoundary</code> component that could occur when untrusted strings were rendered without proper escaping.</p>
<h2>Recommendation</h2>
<p>Users are encouraged to upgrade to this release, especially if they:</p>
<ul>
<li>Use IP Restriction Middleware</li>
<li>Use Cache Middleware on Deno, Bun, or Node.js</li>
<li>Use Serve Static Middleware with user-controlled paths on Cloudflare Workers</li>
<li>Render untrusted data inside <code>ErrorBoundary</code> components</li>
</ul>

Adds `@elizaos/plugin-mintclub` — a plugin for trading [Mint Club V2](https://mint.club) bonding curve tokens on Base.

Only adds `packages/plugin-mintclub/` (5 files) — no other changes.

Enables ElizaOS agents to:
- **Query** token prices, info, and wallet balances
- **Trade** bonding curve tokens with smart routing (auto-picks buy/sell/zap/swap)
- **Swap** any token pair via Uniswap V3/V4

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `TOKEN_INFO` | Get token info (supply, reserve, price, bonding curve) |
| `TOKEN_PRICE` | Get token price in reserve + USD |
| `SWAP` | Smart swap — auto-routes via bonding curve or Uniswap |
| `WALLET_BALANCE` | Show wallet address and balances |

Wraps the [`mint.club-cli`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mint.club-cli) (`mc` command) via shell execution. The CLI handles wallet management, auto routing, ERC-20 approvals, and transaction confirmation.

## Setup

```bash
npm install -g mint.club-cli
```

Set `PRIVATE_KEY` in the agent's environment variables.

<!-- greptile_comment -->

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>


This PR adds persistent database-backed caching to the audio transcription and image description handlers to optimize for Discord bots and other services that frequently process the same media files. The implementation includes:

**Audio transcriptions (`audio.ts`)**:
- Content-based caching using SHA-256 hashing (with fallback) to identify duplicate audio regardless of URL
- Reads audio buffer once for both cache check and API call to avoid redundant I/O
- Best-effort caching that doesn't block requests on cache failures

**Image descriptions (`image.ts`)**:
- URL-based caching for default prompts only (custom prompts bypass cache)
- Image size validation via HEAD request to fail fast on oversized images (>20MB)
- Support for newer model token parameters (`max_completion_tokens` for gpt-5/o1/o3 series)
- Enhanced error handling with detailed error response logging

Both handlers follow a consistent pattern: check cache first, log appropriately, make API call if needed, cache successful results. The caching is designed to be non-intrusive with comprehensive logging for debugging.

<h3>Confidence Score: 4/5</h3>


- This PR is safe to merge with minimal risk - well-designed caching implementation with proper error handling
- Score reflects solid architecture and error handling, but there's a minor cache collision risk in image.ts where different images at the same URL could be cached incorrectly if image content changes without URL change
- Pay attention to `src/models/image.ts` - the URL-based caching could cause issues if image content at a URL changes without the URL changing

<h3>Important Files Changed</h3>




| Filename | Overview |
|----------|----------|
| src/models/audio.ts | Added content-based caching for transcriptions with robust SHA-256 hashing and fallback. Well-designed with proper error handling and detailed documentation. |
| src/models/image.ts | Added URL-based caching, size validation, improved error handling, and max_completion_tokens support for newer models. Minor cache collision risk with URL-only keys. |

</details>



<h3>Sequence Diagram</h3>

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Handler as Audio/Image Handler
    participant Cache as Database Cache
    participant OpenAI as OpenAI API

    Client->>Handler: Request transcription/description
    Handler->>Handler: Prepare media (hash audio/extract URL)
    Handler->>Cache: Check cache with key
    alt Cache HIT
        Cache-->>Handler: Return cached result
        Handler-->>Client: Return result (fast path)
    else Cache MISS
        Cache-->>Handler: No cached result
        Handler->>OpenAI: API request with media
        OpenAI-->>Handler: API response
        Handler->>Cache: Store result (best-effort)
        alt Cache write succeeds
            Cache-->>Handler: Write confirmed
        else Cache write fails
            Cache-->>Handler: Write failed (logged, non-blocking)
        end
        Handler-->>Client: Return result
    end
```

It updates both the build-time template bundling script (`packages/cli/src/scripts/copy-templates.ts`) and the runtime template copier (`packages/cli/src/utils/copy-template.ts`), and adjusts CI/test timeouts plus adds local-development/integration coverage.

- `isPropertyVisible` checked `node.parameters` directly without considering property defaults.             Runtime-->>App: buffer
```mermaid
        else Response is ReadableStream
```

<h2>Greptile Overview</h2>

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

This PR enables per-user MCP server connections in multi-tenant environments by leveraging request context to create isolated connections per entity. It moves `@elizaos/core` to peerDependencies to ensure request context is shared, and implements dynamic API key injection from context into HTTP headers.

**Key Changes:**
- Per-user connection isolation: Connection keys now include entityId for HTTP/SSE transports (e.g., `serverName:entityId`)
- Dynamic API key injection: Reads `ELIZAOS_API_KEY` from request context and injects into `X-API-Key` header for same-origin requests
- Peer dependency change: Moved `@elizaos/core` to peerDependencies to share singleton request context

**Critical Issues Found:**
- Connection key logic fails for eagerly-connected servers: `getConnectionKey()` only checks `lazyConnections` to determine transport type, so eagerly-connected HTTP servers won't get per-user isolation
- `restartConnection` bug: Uses `getConnectionKey()` to get user-specific key but connection may exist under base key, causing disconnect/reconnect to target wrong connection
- Environment variable fallback risk: Origin check defaults to `http://localhost:3000` if env vars aren't set, which could cause issues in production

<h3>Confidence Score: 2/5</h3>

- This PR has critical logic bugs that will break connection management in production multi-tenant deployments
- The per-user isolation feature is well-intentioned but has multiple implementation bugs: getConnectionKey() fails for eagerly-connected HTTP servers, restartConnection() targets wrong connection keys, and environment variable handling is fragile. These issues will cause connection leaks and incorrect routing in production.
- src/service.ts requires immediate attention to fix connection key management logic

<!-- /greptile_comment -->6e:Tf7c,This PR fixes #5216 - EventType.MESSAGE_SENT event not being emitted when agent responses are sent to the central server API.

## Problem

The `sendAgentResponseToBus` function in `packages/server/src/services/message.ts` sends agent responses to the central server API endpoint (`/api/messaging/submit`), but it does not emit the `EventType.MESSAGE_SENT` event.

This means that plugins with handlers for the `MESSAGE_SENT` event never get triggered when messages are submitted to the central channel.

## Solution

Added `EventType.MESSAGE_SENT` event emission after a successful response from the central server API.

## Changes

1. Added `EventType` import from `@elizaos/core`
2. Emit `MESSAGE_SENT` event with proper payload:
   - `runtime`: The agent runtime instance
   - `content`: The message content being sent
   - `roomId`: The room ID where the message was sent
   - `worldId`: The world ID
   - `userId`: The user ID (agent ID in this case)
   - `agentId`: The agent ID

## Testing

All existing tests pass (532 pass, 0 fail).

Closes #5216

<!-- greptile_comment -->

```mermaid
    participant Output as generated-registry.json

    PR->>Index: Add @elizaos/plugin-sportradar entry
    Note over Index: New entry added alphabetically<br/>between plugin-spheron and plugin-sql
    
    Index->>GHA: Trigger on push to main
    GHA->>Script: Execute generate-registry.js
    
    Script->>Index: Read plugin entries
    Script->>GH: Fetch repository metadata
    GH-->>Script: Return repo info (description, topics, stars)
    
    Script->>GH: Get branches (main, 0.x, 1.x)
    GH-->>Script: Return branch list
    
    Script->>GH: Fetch package.json from branches
    GH-->>Script: Return package.json with version info
    
    Script->>GH: Get git tags for versions
    GH-->>Script: Return v0 and v1 tags
    
    Script->>NPM: Query package metadata
    NPM-->>Script: Return published versions
    
    Script->>Script: Analyze version compatibility<br/>Check @elizaos/core dependencies
    
    Script->>Output: Write generated-registry.json
    Note over Output: Includes full metadata:<br/>versions, branches, compatibility,<br/>description, topics
    
    GHA->>Index: Commit updated generated-registry.json
```

Updates `time` from 0.3.45 to 0.3.47
<details>
<summary>Release notes</summary>
<p><em>Sourced from <a href="https://github.com/time-rs/time/releases">time's releases</a>.</em></p>
<blockquote>
<h2>v0.3.47</h2>
<p>See the <a href="https://github.com/time-rs/time/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md">changelog</a> for details.</p>
<h2>v0.3.46</h2>
<p>See the <a href="https://github.com/time-rs/time/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md">changelog</a> for details.</p>
</blockquote>
</details>
<details>
<summary>Changelog</summary>
<p><em>Sourced from <a href="https://github.com/time-rs/time/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md">time's changelog</a>.</em></p>
<blockquote>
<h2>0.3.47 [2026-02-05]</h2>
<h3>Security</h3>
<ul>
<li>
<p>The possibility of a stack exhaustion denial of service attack when parsing RFC 2822 has been
eliminated. Previously, it was possible to craft input that would cause unbounded recursion. Now,
the depth of the recursion is tracked, causing an error to be returned if it exceeds a reasonable
limit.</p>
<p>This attack vector requires parsing user-provided input, with any type, using the RFC 2822 format.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3>Compatibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>Attempting to format a value with a well-known format (i.e. RFC 3339, RFC 2822, or ISO 8601) will
error at compile time if the type being formatted does not provide sufficient information. This
would previously fail at runtime. Similarly, attempting to format a value with ISO 8601 that is
only configured for parsing (i.e. <code>Iso8601::PARSING</code>) will error at compile time.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Added</h3>
<ul>
<li>Builder methods for format description modifiers, eliminating the need for verbose initialization
when done manually.</li>
<li><code>date!(2026-W01-2)</code> is now supported. Previously, a space was required between <code>W</code> and <code>01</code>.</li>
<li><code>[end]</code> now has a <code>trailing_input</code> modifier which can either be <code>prohibit</code> (the default) or
<code>discard</code>. When it is <code>discard</code>, all remaining input is ignored. Note that if there are components
after <code>[end]</code>, they will still attempt to be parsed, likely resulting in an error.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Changed</h3>
<ul>
<li>More performance gains when parsing.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Fixed</h3>
<ul>
<li>If manually formatting a value, the number of bytes written was one short for some components.
This has been fixed such that the number of bytes written is always correct.</li>
<li>The possibility of integer overflow when parsing an owned format description has been effectively
eliminated. This would previously wrap when overflow checks were disabled. Instead of storing the
depth as <code>u8</code>, it is stored as <code>u32</code>. This would require multiple gigabytes of nested input to
overflow, at which point we've got other problems and trivial mitigations are available by
downstream users.</li>
</ul>
<h2>0.3.46 [2026-01-23]</h2>
<h3>Added</h3>
<ul>
<li>All possible panics are now documented for the relevant methods.</li>
<li>The need to use <code>#[serde(default)]</code> when using custom <code>serde</code> formats is documented. This applies
only when deserializing an <code>Option&lt;T&gt;</code>.</li>
<li><code>Duration::nanoseconds_i128</code> has been made public, mirroring
<code>std::time::Duration::from_nanos_u128</code>.</li>
</ul>
<!-- raw HTML omitted -->
</blockquote>
<p>... (truncated)</p>
</details>

</ul>

<h2>Greptile Overview</h2>

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

Updates Rust dependencies across three packages with important security and bug fixes. The `bytes` crate is updated to v1.11.1 (fixes integer overflow in `BytesMut::reserve`), `time` is updated to v0.3.47 (fixes RFC 2822 DoS vulnerability), and `git2` is updated to v0.20.4 (fixes undefined behavior with empty `Buf` dereference).

Key changes:
- **bytes 1.10.1→1.11.1** in `packages/computeruse`: Fixes critical integer overflow, bumps MSRV to 1.57, includes performance improvements
- **bytes 1.11.0→1.11.1** in `packages/rust` and `packages/sweagent/rust`: Applies the integer overflow fix
- **time 0.3.45→0.3.47** in `packages/sweagent/rust`: Eliminates stack exhaustion DoS attack vector in RFC 2822 parsing
- **git2 0.20.3→0.20.4** in `packages/sweagent/rust`: Fixes undefined behavior when dereferencing empty buffers

All updates are patch/minor releases with backward compatibility. The MSRV bump to Rust 1.57 is unlikely to cause issues as it's from 2021.

<h3>Confidence Score: 5/5</h3>

- This PR is safe to merge with minimal risk - it's an automated dependency update with important security fixes
- This is a straightforward Dependabot-generated dependency update that applies security and bug fixes. All updates are to stable, well-maintained crates with no breaking changes. The updates fix real issues (integer overflow, DoS vulnerability, undefined behavior) without introducing new risks.
- No files require special attention - all changes are standard lockfile updates

Updates `time` from 0.3.45 to 0.3.47
<details>
<summary>Release notes</summary>
<p><em>Sourced from <a href="https://github.com/time-rs/time/releases">time's releases</a>.</em></p>
<blockquote>
<h2>v0.3.47</h2>
<p>See the <a href="https://github.com/time-rs/time/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md">changelog</a> for details.</p>
<h2>v0.3.46</h2>
<p>See the <a href="https://github.com/time-rs/time/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md">changelog</a> for details.</p>
</blockquote>
</details>
<details>
<summary>Changelog</summary>
<p><em>Sourced from <a href="https://github.com/time-rs/time/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md">time's changelog</a>.</em></p>
<blockquote>
<h2>0.3.47 [2026-02-05]</h2>
<h3>Security</h3>
<ul>
<li>
<p>The possibility of a stack exhaustion denial of service attack when parsing RFC 2822 has been
eliminated. Previously, it was possible to craft input that would cause unbounded recursion. Now,
the depth of the recursion is tracked, causing an error to be returned if it exceeds a reasonable
limit.</p>
<p>This attack vector requires parsing user-provided input, with any type, using the RFC 2822 format.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3>Compatibility</h3>
<ul>
<li>Attempting to format a value with a well-known format (i.e. RFC 3339, RFC 2822, or ISO 8601) will
error at compile time if the type being formatted does not provide sufficient information. This
would previously fail at runtime. Similarly, attempting to format a value with ISO 8601 that is
only configured for parsing (i.e. <code>Iso8601::PARSING</code>) will error at compile time.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Added</h3>
<ul>
<li>Builder methods for format description modifiers, eliminating the need for verbose initialization
when done manually.</li>
<li><code>date!(2026-W01-2)</code> is now supported. Previously, a space was required between <code>W</code> and <code>01</code>.</li>
<li><code>[end]</code> now has a <code>trailing_input</code> modifier which can either be <code>prohibit</code> (the default) or
<code>discard</code>. When it is <code>discard</code>, all remaining input is ignored. Note that if there are components
after <code>[end]</code>, they will still attempt to be parsed, likely resulting in an error.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Changed</h3>
<ul>
<li>More performance gains when parsing.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Fixed</h3>
<ul>
<li>If manually formatting a value, the number of bytes written was one short for some components.
This has been fixed such that the number of bytes written is always correct.</li>
<li>The possibility of integer overflow when parsing an owned format description has been effectively
eliminated. This would previously wrap when overflow checks were disabled. Instead of storing the
depth as <code>u8</code>, it is stored as <code>u32</code>. This would require multiple gigabytes of nested input to
overflow, at which point we've got other problems and trivial mitigations are available by
downstream users.</li>
</ul>
<h2>0.3.46 [2026-01-23]</h2>
<h3>Added</h3>
<ul>
<li>All possible panics are now documented for the relevant methods.</li>
<li>The need to use <code>#[serde(default)]</code> when using custom <code>serde</code> formats is documented. This applies
only when deserializing an <code>Option&lt;T&gt;</code>.</li>
<li><code>Duration::nanoseconds_i128</code> has been made public, mirroring
<code>std::time::Duration::from_nanos_u128</code>.</li>
</ul>
<!-- raw HTML omitted -->
</blockquote>
<p>... (truncated)</p>
</details>

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

Automated dependency updates bumping `bytes`, `time`, and `git2` libraries across three Rust package directories. All updates include important security fixes:

- **`bytes` 1.11.1**: Fixes integer overflow in `BytesMut::reserve` that could cause memory corruption
- **`time` 0.3.47**: Eliminates stack exhaustion DoS vulnerability in RFC 2822 parsing
- **`git2` 0.20.4**: Fixes undefined behavior when dereferencing empty `Buf`

The changes are limited to lockfile updates and one version constraint bump in `packages/computeruse/crates/computeruse-cli/Cargo.toml` (from `bytes = "1.5"` to `bytes = "1.11"`). All updates are backward-compatible patch/minor version bumps.

- This PR contains only automated dependency updates with critical security fixes. All version bumps are minor/patch releases that maintain backward compatibility. The changes are isolated to lockfiles and one version constraint, with no code modifications required.

<!-- /greptile_comment -->74:T11a0,## Summary

This PR adds defensive null/undefined checks before Object.entries() calls in the @elizaos/core package's settings utilities to prevent runtime errors.

## Changes

### packages/core/src/settings.ts

Added null/undefined guards to the following functions:

1. saltWorldSettings() - Check worldSettings parameter before calling Object.entries()
2. unsaltWorldSettings() - Check worldSettings parameter before calling Object.entries()
3. encryptObjectValues() - Check obj parameter before calling Object.entries()
4. decryptObjectValues() - Check obj parameter before calling Object.entries()

## Problem Solved

These functions are called throughout the codebase with data from database queries and metadata that may be null or undefined. Without these checks, the code throws:

Object.entries requires that input parameter not be null or undefined

This causes providers and handlers to crash, leading to agents ignoring messages.

## Related Issues

- Complements PR #6470 (plugin-bootstrap null checks)
- Fixes same root cause in @elizaos/core package

## Testing

- Functions now return empty objects {} when input is null/undefined instead of crashing
- Maintains backward compatibility - valid inputs continue to work as before
- Safe for all existing call sites that may pass null/undefined values

- Updates `encryptObjectValues`/`decryptObjectValues` similarly to avoid runtime errors when secrets/settings objects are missing.

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

This PR fixes the Claude Code Review workflow failing on fork-based PRs by switching the trigger from `pull_request` to `pull_request_target`, which grants access to OIDC tokens and repository secrets. It also upgrades `pull-requests` and `issues` permissions from `read` to `write` (needed for posting review comments), and adds the `reopened` event type.

- **Security model is sound in principle**: The `actions/checkout@v4` step without an explicit `ref` defaults to the base branch under `pull_request_target`, avoiding checkout of untrusted fork code while secrets are available.
- **Verify `claude-code-action` fetches PR diff via API**: The checkout is the base branch (main), so if the action relies on local file diffs rather than the GitHub API to read PR changes, the review would not see the actual PR content. This should be confirmed.
- The `reopened` event type addition is a minor but useful improvement ensuring reviews re-trigger on reopened PRs.

<h3>Confidence Score: 3/5</h3>

- This PR is likely safe to merge but has a functional concern that should be verified before merging.
- The security model of using `pull_request_target` with a base-branch checkout is the correct pattern. However, it's unclear whether `claude-code-action` will still be able to review the actual PR changes when the checkout is the base branch (main) rather than the PR head. If the action relies on local git state to compute diffs, the review would be non-functional. The permissions and event type changes are straightforward and correct.
- `.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml` — verify that `claude-code-action@beta` fetches PR diffs via GitHub API and does not depend on local checkout containing the PR code.

<!--renovate-config-hash:e80b4e42a3043bc12fa0640db4bac392d2bf770acf841360d7c8ceeeac2ec1a9-->
7a:Ted3,This PR fixes #5707 - an issue where `elizaos agent` commands would fail when connecting to a remote server that uses `ELIZA_SERVER_AUTH_TOKEN`.

## Problem

When running `elizaos agent list` (or other agent commands) against a remote server with authentication enabled via `ELIZA_SERVER_AUTH_TOKEN`, the command would fail with:

```
WARN: Unauthorized access attempt: Missing or invalid X-API-KEY from 127.0.0.1
```

This happened because the CLI was not loading environment variables from `.env` files before making API requests.

## Solution

Added `loadEnvironment()` call at the beginning of the `getAgents()` function in `packages/cli/src/commands/agent/utils/validation.ts`.

This ensures that:
- `.env` files are loaded before API requests
- `ELIZA_SERVER_AUTH_TOKEN` is properly read
- All agent commands (list, get, stop, remove, etc.) work with authenticated servers

## Testing

All existing tests pass (13 pass, 0 fail).

Closes #5707

<!-- greptile_comment -->

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>


This PR fixes authentication issues when running `elizaos agent` commands against a remote server with `ELIZA_SERVER_AUTH_TOKEN` enabled. The fix adds a `loadEnvironment()` call at the beginning of `getAgents()` to ensure `.env` files are loaded before making API requests.

**Key Changes:**
- Added import for `loadEnvironment` from `../../../utils/get-config`
- Added `await loadEnvironment()` call before creating API client config in `getAgents()`
- This ensures `ELIZA_SERVER_AUTH_TOKEN` is available in `process.env` when `createApiClientConfig()` reads it

**Impact:**
- All agent commands (`list`, `get`, `stop`, `remove`, etc.) that use `getAgents()` or `resolveAgentId()` will now properly load environment variables
- Fixes unauthorized access errors when connecting to authenticated servers

<!-- /greptile_comment -->7c:Td49,This PR adds validation to the `ensureDir` function to prevent unclear ENOENT errors when an empty directory path is provided.

## Problem

When `ensureDir` was called with an empty string or whitespace-only path, it would attempt to execute `fs.mkdir('', { recursive: true })`, which results in the cryptic error:

```
ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir
```

This error message doesn't clearly indicate that the problem is an empty directory path.

## Solution

Added validation in the `ensureDir` function to check if the path is empty or contains only whitespace before attempting any filesystem operations.

## Changes

- Added validation: `if (!dirPath || dirPath.trim() === '')`
- Throws clear error: `"Directory path cannot be empty"`
- Validation happens before `existsSync` and `mkdir` calls

## Benefits

1. **Clearer error messages**: Users now get a descriptive error instead of ENOENT
2. **Earlier failure**: Fails fast before attempting filesystem operations
3. **Better debugging**: Makes it obvious when configuration results in empty paths

## Related Issues

This fix helps address issues like #5607 where directory creation fails with unclear errors.

## Testing

The validation is straightforward and will throw an error whenever `ensureDir` is called with an empty or whitespace-only string, preventing the ENOENT error from occurring.

<!-- greptile_comment -->

- Adds validation to `ensureDir` function in `packages/cli/src/utils/get-config.ts` to prevent cryptic ENOENT errors when empty or whitespace-only directory paths are provided
- Replaces unclear filesystem error with descriptive "Directory path cannot be empty" message for better debugging experience

<h3>Important Files Changed</h3>


| Filename | Overview |
|----------|----------|
| packages/cli/src/utils/get-config.ts | Added path validation to prevent ENOENT error when empty directory paths are passed to `ensureDir` function |

```mermaid
    participant CLI as "CLI Application"
    participant ensureDir as "ensureDir Function"

    participant logger as "Logger"

    CLI->>ensureDir: "Call ensureDir(dirPath)"
    ensureDir->>ensureDir: "Check if (!dirPath || dirPath.trim() === '')"
    alt Empty or whitespace-only path
        ensureDir->>CLI: "Throw Error('Directory path cannot be empty')"
    else Valid path provided
        ensureDir->>fs: "Check existsSync(dirPath)"
        alt Directory doesn't exist
            fs->>ensureDir: "Return false"
            ensureDir->>fs: "Call mkdir(dirPath, { recursive: true })"
            fs->>ensureDir: "Directory created successfully"
            ensureDir->>logger: "Log debug message with created directory info"
            ensureDir->>CLI: "Return successfully"
        else Directory already exists
            fs->>ensureDir: "Return true"
            ensureDir->>CLI: "Return successfully"
        end
    end
```

<h2>Greptile Overview</h2>

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

This PR adds defensive validation to the `ensureDir` function in `packages/cli/src/utils/get-config.ts` to prevent ENOENT errors when directory paths are empty or contain only whitespace.

**Key Changes:**
- Added guard clause checking if `dirPath` is empty or contains only whitespace
- Throws clear error message: "Directory path cannot be empty" instead of allowing confusing ENOENT errors from `fs.mkdir`

**Root Cause:**
When environment variables like `PGLITE_DATA_DIR` are set to empty strings (as opposed to being undefined), the nullish coalescing operator (`??`) in `resolvePgliteDir` doesn't skip them, leading to empty paths being passed to `ensureDir`.

**Impact:**
This is a defensive programming fix that improves error messages and prevents runtime crashes. The change is minimal, safe, and directly addresses the issue described in the original PR #6379.

<h3>Confidence Score: 5/5</h3>

- This PR is safe to merge with minimal risk
- The change adds a simple validation check that prevents empty directory paths from causing ENOENT errors. It's a defensive programming practice with clear benefits: better error messages, no breaking changes to existing functionality, and addresses a real edge case where environment variables might be set to empty strings. The fix is minimal (3 lines), well-scoped, and doesn't alter any logic paths for valid inputs.
- No files require special attention

<h3>Important Files Changed</h3>




| Filename | Overview |
|----------|----------|
| packages/cli/src/utils/get-config.ts | Added validation to prevent empty directory paths in `ensureDir`, fixing ENOENT errors when environment variables are set to empty strings |

</details>

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant CLI
    participant getConfig as get-config.ts
    participant ensureDir
    participant fs as Node.js fs

    User->>CLI: Start CLI with empty PGLITE_DATA_DIR env var
    CLI->>getConfig: configureDatabaseSettings()
    getConfig->>getConfig: resolvePgliteDir()
    Note over getConfig: env var = "" (empty string)<br/>fallbackDir is ignored
    getConfig->>getConfig: Returns empty string
    getConfig->>ensureDir: ensureDir("")
    
    alt With PR Fix
        ensureDir->>ensureDir: Check if dirPath is empty/whitespace
        ensureDir-->>getConfig: throw Error("Directory path cannot be empty")
        Note over getConfig: Clear error message
    else Without PR Fix
        ensureDir->>fs: mkdir("", {recursive: true})
```

- SWAP_TOKEN action for executing swaps
- GET_QUOTE for pricing
- x402 payment integration
- Base chain + Uniswap V3

## Package
- npm: micronoise-eliza-plugin
- GitHub: dontonon/micronoise-eliza-plugin
- Demo: micronoise.vercel.app/swap

8b:T5b1,## Context

Eliza is described as "Autonomous agents for everyone" with a massive community (17k+ stars). I'm curious about the multi-agent coordination patterns your users are running into.

## Coordination Scenarios

Do Eliza users ever need:

1. **Multiple Eliza instances coordinating** (different machines, different operators)
2. **Cross-framework agent communication** (Eliza + other agent systems)
3. **Persistent peer relationships** (agent-to-agent trust across sessions)
4. **Capability discovery** (finding agents with specific skills)

## Background

I built [Agora](https://github.com/rookdaemon/agora) to explore this problem space - a coordination protocol for autonomous agents with:

- Cryptographic identity (Ed25519) for persistent agent identities
- Relay-based messaging (WebSocket) that works behind NATs/firewalls
- Peer discovery by capability
- Reputation system for verifying agent outputs

Not promoting, genuinely curious: **is inter-agent coordination a pattern Eliza users need?**

If this is a real use case, I'd be interested in collaborating on integration patterns. Eliza's architecture + Agora's coordination layer could enable some interesting multi-agent scenarios.

## Resources

- Technical guide: https://rookdaemon.github.io/writing/adding-agora-to-your-agent/
- Live relay: `wss://agora-relay.lbsa71.net`
- NPM: `@rookdaemon/agora` v0.2.2

Curious to hear if this resonates with problems your community is solving.8c:Tc5e,# feat(scenarios): Add Cost Evaluator

Links: [Issue #5726](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/5726)

## Summary
Introduce an evaluator that asserts the estimated dollar cost of LLM usage per step. Cost is derived from token counts and a model price table.

## Goals
- Estimate cost (USD) for each step from recorded token metrics
- Allow thresholds (`max_cost_usd`) to fail expensive runs
- Support multiple models within a single step

## Acceptance Criteria
1. New evaluator type `llm_cost`
2. Price table configurable via env or default map
3. Evaluator passes if total step cost <= `max_cost_usd`
4. Detailed message with model breakdown and total

## Schema Changes
Edit `packages/cli/src/commands/scenario/src/schema.ts`:

```ts
const LlmCostEvaluationSchema = BaseEvaluationSchema.extend({
  type: z.literal('llm_cost'),
  max_cost_usd: z.number(),
});
```

## Pricing Source
Add a small utility `packages/cli/src/commands/scenario/src/pricing.ts`:

```ts
export type ModelPricing = {
  inputPer1K: number;    // USD per 1000 input tokens
  outputPer1K: number;   // USD per 1000 output tokens
};

export const DEFAULT_MODEL_PRICING: Record<string, ModelPricing> = {
  TEXT_SMALL: { inputPer1K: 0.15, outputPer1K: 0.60 },
  TEXT_LARGE: { inputPer1K: 0.50, outputPer1K: 1.50 },
  OBJECT_SMALL: { inputPer1K: 0.50, outputPer1K: 1.50 },
};

export function getPricing(modelType: string, overrides?: Record<string, ModelPricing>): ModelPricing | null {
  const table = overrides ?? DEFAULT_MODEL_PRICING;
  return table[modelType] ?? null;
}
```

Allow overrides via `SCENARIO_MODEL_PRICING` env (JSON string) in a follow-up.

## Evaluation Implementation
Add to `EvaluationEngine`:

```ts
class LlmCostEvaluator implements Evaluator {
  async evaluate(params: EvaluationSchema, runResult: ExecutionResult): Promise<EvaluationResult> {
    if (params.type !== 'llm_cost') throw new Error('Mismatched evaluator');
    const llm = runResult.metrics?.llm ?? [];
    if (!llm.length) return { success: false, message: 'No LLM metrics found for cost calculation' };

    const pricingOverrides = process.env.SCENARIO_MODEL_PRICING ? JSON.parse(process.env.SCENARIO_MODEL_PRICING) : undefined;
    let total = 0;
    for (const m of llm) {
      const pricing = getPricing(m.modelType, pricingOverrides);
      if (!pricing) continue;
      const inTok = m.promptTokens ?? 0;
      const outTok = m.completionTokens ?? 0;
      total += (inTok / 1000) * pricing.inputPer1K + (outTok / 1000) * pricing.outputPer1K;
    }

    const success = total <= params.max_cost_usd;
    return { success, message: `Estimated cost: $${total.toFixed(4)} (limit $${params.max_cost_usd.toFixed(4)})` };
  }
}
```

Register:

```ts
this.register('llm_cost', new LlmCostEvaluator());
```

## Example Usage

```yaml
evaluations:
  - type: llm_cost
    max_cost_usd: 0.05
```

## Tests
- Unit: price math with multiple model records
- Integration: with token_count metrics present and absent

## Notes
This builds on the Token Count evaluator and shared metrics capture. It complements mocking enhancements described in [Issue #5726](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/5726).

/cc @NaniLabs8f:T448,## Description
When a user sends a message containing a URL, ElizaOS processes it twice:
1. As text content → generates response
2. As attachment (metadata/preview) → generates second response

Both responses are sent through the same SSE stream before the `done` event, resulting in duplicated text in the final response.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start ElizaOS with webapp
2. Send a message containing a URL (e.g., "Check this: https://example.com")
3. Observe the response

## Expected Behavior
URL should be processed once, generating a single response.

## Actual Behavior
Two identical (or near-identical) responses are generated and streamed as one message, doubling token usage and producing duplicated output.

## Impact
- 2x LLM API calls per message with URL
- Doubled token costs
- Poor UX with duplicated responses
- Forces workarounds on client side

## Environment
- ElizaOS version: [your version]
- Client: webapp

## Suggested Fix
Ensure URL is processed either as text OR as attachment, not both. The decision should happen in the message processing flow before LLM calls.

The current OpenAI provider does **not support configuring a custom OpenAI endpoint URL**, which makes it impossible to use OpenAI-compatible third-party services (e.g., SiliconFlow). These services follow the OpenAI API format but require pointing to their own endpoint URLs instead of the official OpenAI endpoint.

## Describe alternatives you've considered
- Switching to a dedicated provider for SiliconFlow: Not ideal, as it breaks the unified OpenAI-compatible usage pattern.
- Hardcoding the endpoint: Not flexible for different OpenAI-compatible providers.

## Additional context
Many cloud / inference providers (SiliconFlow, etc.) provide OpenAI-compatible APIs, only differing in the endpoint URL. Supporting custom endpoints will greatly improve the compatibility and flexibility of the OpenAI provider.91:T84a,## Summary

[MoltBridge](https://moltbridge.ai) provides trust-verified agent discovery — cryptographic identity, a trust graph, and broker-mediated warm introductions between AI agents. We'd like to build an **official ElizaOS plugin** that gives Eliza agents the ability to discover and verify other agents through this trust infrastructure.

## Why This Fits ElizaOS

ElizaOS thrives on its plugin ecosystem. MoltBridge would be a plugin that adds:

1. **Agent Discovery**: Eliza agents can search for other agents by capability (e.g., "find a trusted code review agent") through MoltBridge's broker registry
2. **Cryptographic Identity**: Each Eliza agent gets a verifiable identity (Ed25519 keypair) that persists across sessions and platforms
3. **Trust Attestations**: After collaborating, agents can attest to each other's capabilities — building a trust graph that makes future introductions more reliable
4. **Warm Introductions**: Instead of cold-connecting to unknown agents, Eliza agents get broker-mediated introductions through mutual trust paths

## Technical Integration

MoltBridge exposes a REST API with SDKs for [JavaScript](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@moltbridge/sdk) and [Python](https://pypi.org/project/moltbridge/). The ElizaOS plugin would:

- Register the Eliza agent on MoltBridge during initialization (with Ed25519 keypair generation)
- Expose MoltBridge actions (discover, attest, request-introduction) as Eliza plugin actions
- Handle trust attestation flows after agent-to-agent interactions
- Support the A2A protocol for cross-framework agent communication

## Cultural Alignment

ElizaOS's Web3/crypto DNA and MoltBridge's cryptographic identity model share the same philosophical foundation: verifiable, decentralized trust without central gatekeepers.

## Links

- API: https://api.moltbridge.ai
- Docs: https://moltbridge.ai/docs
- Research: https://moltbridge.ai/research

When an Eliza agent sends USDC or ETH through `IWalletService`, it has no signal about whether the recipient wallet is trustworthy. A fresh sybil wallet created 3 hours ago looks identical to a 6-month-old legitimate operator.

This matters more for autonomous agents than for humans — agents can't "eyeball" a wallet's history on a block explorer before sending money.

### Proposal

Add an optional pre-transfer reputation check using [DJD Agent Score](https://djd-agent-score.fly.dev), a free API that scores wallets on Base based on on-chain USDC transaction history.

This could be implemented as a skill or as a guard in the wallet service:

```typescript
// Skill: check wallet reputation before sending money
async function checkWalletReputation(wallet: string): Promise<{
  safe: boolean;
  score: number;
  tier: string;
  reason: string;
}> {
  const res = await fetch(
    `https://djd-agent-score.fly.dev/v1/score/basic?wallet=${wallet}`
  );
  const { score, tier, confidence, recommendation } = await res.json();

  return {
    safe: score >= 40 && confidence >= 0.2,
    score,
    tier,
    reason: score < 40
      ? `Low reputation (${score}/100, ${tier}) — wallet may be newly created or show suspicious patterns`
      : `Reputation OK (${score}/100, ${tier})`
  };
}
```

### What the scoring covers

The API analyzes real on-chain USDC transaction history and runs 12 behavioral checks:

- **Sybil detection** — closed-loop trading, puppet funding chains, coordinated wallet creation
- **Gaming detection** — wash trading, velocity spikes, balance window dressing
- **Identity signals** — account age, Basename registration, partner diversity
- **Reliability** — transaction consistency, payment patterns

Returns a 0–100 score with tier (New/Developing/Emerging/Established/Trusted), confidence level, and recommendation.

### Why this fits Eliza

- **Free tier**: 10 calls/day, no API key, no signup — zero friction for agent developers
- **Fast**: <200ms response, cached scores
- **TypeScript native**: Simple `fetch()` call, typed responses
- **On-chain data only**: No off-chain identity required — works for any wallet on Base
- **Eliza's wallet system**: Agents using `IWalletService` to send transactions can check recipients before transferring

This ticket proposes an enhancement to the `llm_judge` evaluator to support a multi-level evaluation scale (e.g., `FAIL`, `PARTIAL PASS`, `PASS`). This will enable more granular and realistic testing of LLM behavior, providing more insightful feedback on an agent's performance. It allows scenario creators to define what constitutes a full pass versus a partial one, leading to more sophisticated agent evaluations.

#### **Acceptance Criteria**

1.  The `LLMJudgeEvaluationSchema` in `packages/cli/src/scenarios/schema.ts` is updated to allow the `expected` field to be an array of strings, representing the possible evaluation levels (e.g., `['FAIL', 'PARTIAL', 'PASS']`).
2.  The `LLMJudgeEvaluator` in `packages/cli/src/scenarios/EvaluationEngine.ts` is refactored to instruct the LLM judge to respond with one of the provided evaluation levels.
3.  The `EvaluationResult` interface is updated to include the specific `level` (e.g., 'PARTIAL') returned by an evaluator, in addition to the overall `success` boolean.
4.  The `Reporter` class in `packages/cli/src/scenarios/Reporter.ts` is updated to display the evaluation level in its output, using distinct icons and colors for each level (e.g., ✅ PASS, 🟠 PARTIAL, ❌ FAIL).
5.  The final `judgment` logic in `packages/cli/src/commands/scenario.ts` is enhanced to accommodate the new levels. For example, an `all_pass` strategy should require all evaluations to achieve the highest success level (e.g., 'PASS').
6.  The process exit code logic remains `0` for an overall scenario pass and `1` for a fail, based on the final judgment.

#### **Technical Approach**

**1. Update Scenario Schema (`schema.ts`)**

```typescript
  prompt: z.string(),
  // Change from z.string() to z.array(z.string()) to define the evaluation scale.
  // Default to a binary scale if not provided.
  expected: z.array(z.string()).optional().default(['FAIL', 'PASS']),
});
// ...
```

**2. Refactor Evaluation Engine (`EvaluationEngine.ts`)**

The `LLMJudgeEvaluator` must be updated to pass the new evaluation scale to the LLM. The general `EvaluationResult` type will also be updated to include the `level`.

```typescript
// packages/cli/src/scenarios/EvaluationEngine.ts
// ...
export interface EvaluationResult {
    success: boolean; // True if not the lowest evaluation level
    level: string;    // The specific outcome, e.g., 'PASS', 'FAIL', 'PARTIAL'
    message: string;
}

interface Evaluator {
    // This method will now return the string level of the outcome.
    evaluate(runtime: IAgentRuntime, result: ScenarioResult): Promise<string>;
    getMessage(level: string): string;
    // Helper to get the expected levels
    getLevels(): string[];
}

class LLMJudgeEvaluator implements Evaluator {
    constructor(private prompt: string, private expected: string[]) {}

    async evaluate(runtime: IAgentRuntime, result: ScenarioResult): Promise<string> {
        const systemPrompt = `You are an AI assistant that judges the output of a command. Based on the prompt and the command output, respond with ONLY one of the following values: [${this.expected.join(', ')}].`;

        const llmResult = await runtime.useModel('TEXT_LARGE', {
            system: systemPrompt,
            messages: [{
                role: 'user',
                content: `Prompt: ${this.prompt}\nOutput: ${result.stdout}`
            }]
        });
        
        const response = llmResult.trim().toUpperCase();
        // Validate the LLM's response against the expected levels.
        if (this.expected.map(e => e.toUpperCase()).includes(response)) {
            return response;
        }
        // Default to the first (lowest) level if the LLM's response is invalid.
        return this.expected[0].toUpperCase();
    }
    
    getLevels(): string[] {
        return this.expected;
    }
    // ... getMessage remains similar ...
}

export class EvaluationEngine {
    // ...
    async run(runtime: IAgentRuntime, result: ScenarioResult): Promise<EvaluationResult[]> {
        const results: EvaluationResult[] = [];
        for (const evaluator of this.evaluators) {
            const level = await evaluator.evaluate(runtime, result);
            const levels = evaluator.getLevels();
            // "Success" is defined as any outcome that is not the lowest possible level.
            const success = level !== levels[0].toUpperCase();
            results.push({ success, level, message: evaluator.getMessage(level) });
        }
        return results;
    }
}
```

```typescript
    // ...

// ...
```

    *   **Verify**: The reporter shows `✅ PASS`, the final status is `✅ PASS`, and the exit code is `0`.94:Te73,### Problem Statement
Currently, ElizaOS scenario testing lacks the ability to mock internal agent runtime calls (particularly LLM interactions) when testing via the API client. This makes it difficult to create deterministic tests for agent behavior and workflows.

### Current Limitations
- Global function mocks only work for code executed in the same process
- No way to intercept `runtime.useModel` calls from the bootstrap plugin
- Agent behavior is non-deterministic due to real LLM calls
- Difficult to test specific agent decision paths and responses

### Why Different Approach Was Needed

The existing mocking system was designed for **code execution environments** (E2B sandbox and local `node -e` processes), where mocks are applied to the execution context. However, **agent testing** works differently:

- **E2B/Local Execution**: Code runs in isolated processes/sandboxes where global mocks can be applied
- **Agent Testing**: Agent runs as a service with API client interaction, requiring direct runtime method interception
- **Architecture Gap**: The bootstrap plugin calls `runtime.useModel` internally, which can't be mocked through the execution environment approach

This architectural difference necessitated a new approach that directly intercepts runtime methods rather than relying on execution context mocking.

### Proposed Solution: Runtime Method Mocking

We've implemented a new mocking approach that directly intercepts `IAgentRuntime` method calls:

#### Key Components

1. **MockEngine Enhancement**
   - Added `runtimeMethodMocks` to support mocking runtime methods
   - Priority system: `runtimeMethod` > `service` > `globalFunction`
   - Direct method replacement on the runtime instance

2. **Schema Updates**
   - Extended `MockSchema` to include `runtimeMethod: z.string().optional()`
   - Supports mocking any `IAgentRuntime` method (e.g., `useModel`, `getService`)

3. **Conditional Matching**
   - Matcher functions can inspect method arguments
   - Example: `"return args[1] && args[1].prompt && args[1].prompt.includes('should respond')"`
   - Supports complex conditional logic for when to apply mocks

#### Usage Example

```yaml
setup:
  mocks:
    - runtimeMethod: "useModel"
      method: "useModel"
      when:
        matcher: "return args[1] && args[1].prompt && args[1].prompt.includes('should respond')"
      response: "<response><name>agent</name><reasoning>Mocked response</reasoning><action>RESPOND</action></response>"
```

#### Benefits

1. **Deterministic Testing**: Replace LLM calls with static responses
2. **Full Workflow Testing**: Test complete agent decision flows
3. **Conditional Mocking**: Apply mocks based on specific conditions
4. **Runtime Integration**: Works seamlessly with existing agent architecture
5. **Backward Compatibility**: Existing mocks continue to work

#### Implementation Steps

- MockEngine runtime method support
- Schema updates for runtimeMethod mocks
- Conditional matching with matcher functions
- Integration with scenario runner
- Basic useModel mocking working
- Add support for mocking other runtime methods (getService, etc.)
- Create comprehensive test scenarios
- Add documentation and examples
- Consider adding mock recording/replay capabilities

### Technical Details

The implementation works by:
1. Creating the `IAgentRuntime` instance in the scenario runner
2. Applying mocks directly to the runtime object before agent initialization
3. The bootstrap plugin receives the mocked runtime and uses the mocked methods
4. Mocks are reverted after scenario completion

This approach provides the foundation for robust, deterministic agent testing while maintaining the existing architecture.95:Tb74,# feat(scenarios): Add Step Count Evaluator

Links: [Issue #5726](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/5726)

## Summary
Add an evaluator that asserts on the number of agent/tool/action steps taken to complete a scenario step. This encourages concise trajectories and prevents thrashing.

## Goals
- Count actions/tools invoked during response generation for a step
- Assert against `max_steps`, `min_steps`, optional `target_steps`

## Acceptance Criteria
1. New evaluator type `step_count`
2. Step count derived from trajectory/action memories queried via `AgentRuntime.getMemories`
3. Evaluator passes if within bounds and returns a clear message

## Schema Changes
Edit `packages/cli/src/commands/scenario/src/schema.ts`:

```ts
const StepCountEvaluationSchema = BaseEvaluationSchema.extend({
  type: z.literal('step_count'),
  max_steps: z.number().optional(),
  min_steps: z.number().optional(),
  target_steps: z.number().optional(),
  // optional filter by action name prefix to scope counting
  action_prefix: z.string().optional(),
});
```

## Evaluation Implementation
Leverage the existing `TrajectoryContainsActionEvaluator` patterns.

```ts
class StepCountEvaluator implements Evaluator {
  async evaluate(params: EvaluationSchema, _runResult: ExecutionResult, runtime: AgentRuntime): Promise<EvaluationResult> {
    if (params.type !== 'step_count') throw new Error('Mismatched evaluator');
    try {
      const memories = await runtime.getMemories({
        tableName: 'messages', agentId: runtime.agentId, count: 200, unique: false,
      });
      const actionResults = memories.filter(m => m?.type === 'messages' && m.content?.type === 'action_result');
      const filtered = params.action_prefix
        ? actionResults.filter(m => (m.content?.actionName ?? '').startsWith(params.action_prefix!))
        : actionResults;
      const steps = filtered.length;

      const tooMany = params.max_steps != null && steps > params.max_steps;
      const tooFew = params.min_steps != null && steps < params.min_steps;
      const success = !(tooMany || tooFew);
      return {
        success,
        message: `Steps taken: ${steps} (min=${params.min_steps ?? '-'}, target=${params.target_steps ?? '-'}, max=${params.max_steps ?? '-'})`,
      };
    } catch (error: any) {
      return { success: false, message: `Step count evaluation failed: ${error.message ?? String(error)}` };
    }
  }
}
```

Register in `EvaluationEngine` constructor:

```ts
this.register('step_count', new StepCountEvaluator());
```

## Example Usage

```yaml
evaluations:
  - type: step_count
    max_steps: 3
    action_prefix: "github-service."
```

## Tests
- Unit: evaluator result on synthetic memories
- Integration: scenario that triggers 1-2 simple actions and validates bound

## Notes
- Future enhancement: count only steps within the current scenario step window by tagging messages with a scenario/step id context field.


96:Tdbc,# feat(scenarios): Add Consistency Evaluator

Links: [Issue #5726](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/5726)

## Summary
Add an evaluator that runs the same step multiple times and asserts consistency over a chosen metric (response content, length, execution time, token counts). Useful for detecting non-determinism and regression in prompt/rules.

## Goals
- Re-run a step N times
- Compare result metrics across runs
- Allow tolerance configuration

## Acceptance Criteria
1. New evaluator type `consistency_check`
2. Supports metrics: `response_length` | `execution_time` | `token_count`
3. Configurable `runs` (>=2) and `tolerance` (absolute or percentage)
4. Consolidated pass/fail with clear variance message

## Schema Changes
Edit `packages/cli/src/commands/scenario/src/schema.ts`:

```ts
const ConsistencyEvaluationSchema = BaseEvaluationSchema.extend({
  type: z.literal('consistency_check'),
  runs: z.number().min(2),
  metric: z.enum(['response_length', 'execution_time', 'token_count']),
  tolerance: z.number().min(0), // if < 1 treat as proportion, else absolute
});
```

## Orchestration Changes
Add a helper to re-execute the current step within the selected environment provider without re-running the entire scenario:

- Expose a `runSingleStep(step, scenarioContext)` on providers that mirrors the logic in `run`, returning an `ExecutionResult`.
- In `EvaluationEngine`, when encountering `consistency_check`, call this helper to collect multiple `ExecutionResult`s for the same step.
- Fallback: If helper is not implemented, re-run `run([step])` via a shim.

## Evaluation Implementation

```ts
class ConsistencyEvaluator implements Evaluator {
  constructor(private rerunStep: (times: number) => Promise<ExecutionResult[]>) {}

  async evaluate(params: EvaluationSchema, runResult: ExecutionResult): Promise<EvaluationResult> {
    if (params.type !== 'consistency_check') throw new Error('Mismatched evaluator');

    const runs = await this.rerunStep(params.runs);
    const values = runs.map(r => {
      switch (params.metric) {
        case 'response_length': return r.stdout.length;
        case 'execution_time': return r.durationMs ?? 0;
        case 'token_count': {
          const llm = r.metrics?.llm ?? [];
          return llm.reduce((sum, m) => sum + (m.totalTokens ?? (m.promptTokens ?? 0) + (m.completionTokens ?? 0)), 0);
        }
      }
    });

    const min = Math.min(...values);
    const max = Math.max(...values);
    const spread = max - min;
    const baseline = values[0] || 1;
    const proportion = baseline ? spread / baseline : spread;
    const threshold = params.tolerance < 1 ? params.tolerance : params.tolerance / baseline;
    const success = proportion <= threshold;

    return {
      success,
      message: `Consistency ${success ? 'ok' : 'failed'} for ${params.metric}: min=${min}, max=${max}, spread=${spread}, tolerance=${params.tolerance}`,
    };
  }
}
```

Register in `EvaluationEngine` with a provider-specific `rerunStep` function wired from the scenario runner.

## Example Usage

```yaml
evaluations:
  - type: consistency_check
    runs: 3
    metric: execution_time
    tolerance: 0.2   # 20% spread allowed
```

## Tests
- Unit: evaluator math on synthetic values
- Integration: deterministic small prompt with low tolerance; non-deterministic with higher tolerance

## Notes
- This evaluator requires access to the step context. Implementation will pass a `rerunStep(times)` closure into the evaluator at construction time.

- Track token counts for LLM interactions triggered by a step

3. Evaluator passes if counts are within configured maxima

## Schema Changes
Edit `packages/cli/src/commands/scenario/src/schema.ts`:

```ts
const TokenCountEvaluationSchema = BaseEvaluationSchema.extend({

  max_input_tokens: z.number().optional(),
  max_output_tokens: z.number().optional(),
  max_total_tokens: z.number().optional(),
});

// Add to EvaluationSchema union
```

## Runtime Integration
We will attach a per-step metrics accumulator that the evaluators can read via `ExecutionResult` metadata. Minimal, provider-agnostic approach:

### ExecutionResult extension
Edit `packages/cli/src/commands/scenario/src/providers.ts`:

```ts
export interface ExecutionResult {
  // ...existing
  metrics?: {
    llm?: Array<{
      modelType: string;
      promptTokens?: number;
      completionTokens?: number;
      totalTokens?: number;
      provider?: string;
    }>;
  };
}
```

### Capturing tokens
Add a light hook layer around `AgentRuntime.useModel` during scenario runs:

- In `runtime-factory.ts`, wrap the runtime instance for scenarios with a proxy that:
  - Intercepts `useModel`
  - If params include a prompt or known text fields, call tokenizer via `ModelType.TEXT_TOKENIZER_ENCODE` to estimate prompt tokens
  - After result, estimate output tokens similarly
  - Push a record into `currentStepMetrics.llm[]`

Note: If a tokenizer is not available, fall back to heuristic length/4 estimate. Keep it optional so normal runs are unaffected.

## Evaluation Implementation
Add to `EvaluationEngine`:

```ts
class TokenCountEvaluator implements Evaluator {
  async evaluate(params: EvaluationSchema, runResult: ExecutionResult): Promise<EvaluationResult> {
    if (params.type !== 'token_count') throw new Error('Mismatched evaluator');
    const llm = runResult.metrics?.llm ?? [];
    if (!llm.length) {
      return { success: false, message: 'No LLM token metrics found for this step' };
    }
    const totals = llm.reduce((acc, m) => ({
      prompt: acc.prompt + (m.promptTokens ?? 0),
      completion: acc.completion + (m.completionTokens ?? 0),
      total: acc.total + (m.totalTokens ?? ((m.promptTokens ?? 0) + (m.completionTokens ?? 0))),
    }), { prompt: 0, completion: 0, total: 0 });

    const tooManyInput = params.max_input_tokens != null && totals.prompt > params.max_input_tokens;
    const tooManyOutput = params.max_output_tokens != null && totals.completion > params.max_output_tokens;
    const tooManyTotal = params.max_total_tokens != null && totals.total > params.max_total_tokens;

    const success = !(tooManyInput || tooManyOutput || tooManyTotal);
    return {
      success,
      message: `Tokens — input:${totals.prompt}, output:${totals.completion}, total:${totals.total}`,
    };
  }
}
```

Register in constructor:

```ts
this.register('token_count', new TokenCountEvaluator());
```

## Example Usage

```yaml

  - type: token_count
    max_input_tokens: 2000
    max_output_tokens: 1000
    max_total_tokens: 2500
```

- Unit: evaluator aggregation logic
- Integration: scenario with a small prompt + enforced limits; tokenizer present and absent

- This is complementary to a Cost evaluator which can derive cost from token metrics and model price tables.

- [ ] Response time < 3 seconds targetae:T583,# Add Verifiable Audit Trail Plugin (VAL)

**Problem:**
Eliza agents need verifiable, tamper-proof records of their actions. Current logs are mutable and local-only - users must trust the agent operator.

**Proposed Solution:**
Add VAL (Verifiable Agent Log) plugin that automatically attests agent actions to immutable storage (Hedera HCS by default, works on any chain).

**Example Usage:**
```typescript
import { VALPlugin } from '@elizaos/plugin-val';

const agent = new Agent({
  name: "MyAgent",
  plugins: [
    new VALPlugin({ topicId: "0.0.12345" })
  ]
});

// Every action is now attested to HCS - immutable & publicly verifiable
```

**Benefits:**
- **Trust**: Users can verify agent behavior independently
- **Transparency**: Public audit trail of all actions
- **Security**: Detect if agent behavior changes unexpectedly
- **Compliance**: Auditable records for regulated use cases

**Why This Fits Eliza's Philosophy:**
Eliza is about building agents "in the open" - VAL makes that transparency cryptographically verifiable. Every action is provable, not just claimed.

**Specification:**
https://github.com/aite550659-max/verifiable-agent-log

**Reference Implementation:**
https://github.com/aite550659-max/verifiable-agent-log/tree/main/integrations/eliza

**Cost:** ~$0.0008 per attestation (~$30/year for 100 actions/day)

Would love to contribute this as an official Eliza plugin. Thoughts?

SAID is on-chain identity infrastructure for AI agents on Solana. Think of it as a universal agent passport — verifiable identity, reputation scores, skill listings, and agent-to-agent discovery.

# Relates to

Relates to #6486

# Risks

Low — single condition removed from a boolean expression. No new code, no new logic paths.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Removes the `providers.length` check from the `isSimple` determination in `packages/typescript/src/services/message.ts`.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue).

# Changes

When a user sends a message containing a URL, the LLM's first call (via `runSingleShotCore`) generates and streams the response text. It also returns `providers: ["ATTACHMENTS"]` because the prompt template instructs it to when it sees URLs.

The `isSimple` check at line 1883 previously treated "has providers" as "not simple":

```typescript
const isSimple =
    responseContent?.actions &&
    responseContent.actions.length === 1 &&
    typeof responseContent.actions[0] === "string" &&
    responseContent.actions[0].toUpperCase() === "REPLY" &&
    (!responseContent.providers || responseContent.providers.length === 0);
//   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
//   This condition causes the bug
```

This caused the message to go through the `actions` path, which triggered the REPLY action handler (`reply.ts:60`), making a **second LLM call** with `replyTemplate` and streaming another response — duplicating output and doubling token costs.

**The fix:** Remove the providers check. Providers enrich state (already handled at L863-871) but don't require re-generating the response. `isSimple` should only care about whether the action is REPLY (text already generated and streamed) vs something else (needs execution).

```typescript
const isSimple =
    responseContent?.actions &&
    responseContent.actions.length === 1 &&
    typeof responseContent.actions[0] === "string" &&
    responseContent.actions[0].toUpperCase() === "REPLY";
```

# Testing

- [x] Message with URL → single response (not duplicated)
- [x] Message without URL → works as before
- [x] Multi-action messages (REPLY + other) → still trigger actions path
- [x] Messages with non-REPLY actions → still trigger actions path

Fixes critical runtime errors in `plugin-bootstrap` providers when metadata or values are null/undefined.

## Problem

The agent crashes with the error:
```
Object.entries requires that input parameter not be null or undefined
```

This occurs in several providers:
1. **relationshipsProvider**: When `entity.metadata` is null/undefined
2. **actionStateProvider**: When `result.values` or `workingMemory` are not objects
3. **recentMessagesProvider**: Similar issues with null values

## Solution

Added proper null/undefined checks before calling `Object.entries()`:

### 1. `src/providers/relationships.ts`
- Added null/undefined check in `formatMetadata()`
- Returns `'{}'` for null/undefined metadata instead of crashing

### 2. `src/providers/actionState.ts`  
- Added type check for `result.values` before calling `Object.entries()`
- Added type/null check for `workingMemory` before calling `Object.keys()`

## Changes

- **packages/plugin-bootstrap/src/providers/relationships.ts**: Guard `formatMetadata()` against null metadata
- **packages/plugin-bootstrap/src/providers/actionState.ts**: Add type guards for `result.values` and `workingMemory`

## Testing

1. Started ElizaOS agent
2. Sent messages via web interface (http://localhost:3000)
3. Verified no more `Object.entries` errors
4. Confirmed agent responds properly instead of showing IGNORE action

## Impact

- ✅ Prevents agent crashes when entities have null metadata
- ✅ Improves stability for action result processing
- ✅ Fixes "IGNORE" action issue when agent can't retrieve conversation context
- ✅ No breaking changes - only adds safety checks

```mermaid
    Runtime->>Database: Create memory

    Runtime->>Runtime: Check request context
    alt Entity-specific setting exists
        Runtime-->>User: Return entity setting
    else No entity setting
        Runtime->>Runtime: Fall back to agent setting
        Runtime-->>User: Return agent setting
    end
```
